'''Raúl Jiménez Tellado''' (born 10 January 1967), known professionally as '''Raul Jimenez''', is a Spanish cosmologist and theoretical physicist and currently the [[Catalan Institution for Research and Advanced Studies|ICREA]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.icrea.cat/|title=ICREA|website=www.icrea.cat}}</ref> Professor of Cosmology at the [[University of Barcelona]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://icc.ub.edu/|title=ICCUB|website=icc.ub.edu}}</ref> His research interests include the origin and evolution of the [[Universe]], [[Large-scale structure of the Cosmos|large-scale structure]], [[dark matter]], [[dark energy]], [[inflation (cosmology)|inflation]], the [[cosmic microwave background]], [[statistics]] and [[Bayesian inference]].

== Early life, education, and career ==
Jimenez was born in [[Madrid]], Spain, in 1967 in the [[:es:barrio de Salamanca|Salamanca District]] where he also grew up. He attended elementary and middle school at the Colegio Publico Ntra. Sea. de la Almudena.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.educa2.madrid.org/web/centro.cp.almudena.madrid#ad-image-0|title=Colegio Publico Ntra. sra. de la Almudena}}</ref>  He completed his high school education at the [[:es:Instituto de Bachillerato Cervantes|Instituto de Bachillerato Cervantes]] in the natural sciences branch, and completed his undergraduate studies at the [[Universidad Autonoma de Madrid]] specializing in theoretical physics. He obtained his Ph.D. in 1995 at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]] of the [[University of Copenhagen]].

He then moved to the [[Royal Observatory, Edinburgh|Royal Observatory]] in Edinburgh, where he held a PPARC Advanced Fellowship. After this five-year period, he went to the U.S. where he joined the faculty of the Physics & Astronomy departments of [[Rutgers University]] and, later, the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. He joined [[Catalan Institution for Research and Advanced Studies|ICREA]] in September 2007 as a Professor.

== Astronomical research ==
Jimenez is a cosmologist and works on theoretical cosmology and astrophysics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/site/rauljimenez|title=Raul Jimenez|website=sites.google.com}}</ref> He uses astronomical observations to learn about the fundamental laws of nature. His research interests are broad and range from the origin and evolution of the universe to the physics of stars and stellar systems. He is also interested in large scale structures and the theory behind them. He has made several contributions to the analysis of large datasets and the introduction of Bayesian statistics in cosmology. His most cited papers are:

J Simon, L Verde, R Jimenez "Constraints of the redshift dependence of the dark energy profile", [[Physical Review|''Physical Review D'']] 71 (12), 123001 (905 Google Scholar citations)

D Stern, R Jimenez, L Verde, M Kamionkowski, SA Stanford "Cosmic chronometers: constraining the equation of state of dark energy. I: H (z) measurements" ''[[Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics]]'' 2010 (02), 008 (739 citations)

A Heavens, B Panter, R Jimenez, J Dunlop -"The star-formation history of the Universe from the stellar populations of nearby galaxies" ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'', 2004 (555 citations)

His research has been featured in several public outlets like ''New Scientist'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg15621022-500-invisible-worlds/|title=Invisible worlds|first=Marcus|last=Chown|website=New Scientist}}</ref> ''Le Point'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lepoint.fr/astronomie/vie-extraterrestre-plus-seuls-que-prevu-dans-l-univers-08-12-2014-1887702_1925.php|title=Vie extraterrestre : plus seuls que prévu dans l'Univers ?|first=Chloé|last=Durand-Parenti|date=8 December 2014|website=Le Point}}</ref> ''The Economist'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.economist.com/science-and-technology/2014/10/16/bolts-from-the-blue|title=Bolts from the blue|via=The Economist}}</ref> and ''Forbes''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/startswithabang/2016/07/13/could-dark-energy-be-caused-by-frozen-neutrinos/|title=Could Dark Energy Be Caused By Frozen Neutrinos?|first=Ethan|last=Siegel|website=Forbes}}</ref>

==Other work==
His book ''Democracias Robotizadas'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.catarata.org/libro/democracias-robotizadas_80852/| title = Democracias Robotizadas}}</ref> written with sociologist [[Luis Moreno Fernández]] has been translated to English<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07K27H7GW/ref=dp-kindle-redirect?_encoding=UTF8&btkr=1| title = Robotized Democracies}}</ref> and Italian.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aracneeditrice.it/index.php/pubblicazione.html?item=9788825520651| title = Democracie Robotizzate}}</ref> It gives a description of the current and future technologies employed in the development of machine learning and artificial intelligence, and elaborates on how our democracies can survive the progressive and inevitable robotization of our societies.

In his new book ''Behind Closed Doors'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/Behind-Closed-Doors-Changes-Pandemic/dp/B095HTP4ZX/ref=sr_1_1?dchild=1&keywords=behind+closed+doors+luis+moreno&qid=1623755216&sr=8-1| title = Behind Closed Doors}}</ref> he reflects on the role that robotization, machine learning and big data had during the pandemic and how our society needs to adjust to the new reality of massive virtualization.

==Honors and awards==
Among other honors, Raul Jimenez was a [[Institut Henri Poincaré|Henri Poincaré Institute]]/[[CNRS]] distinguished visiting professor in the Fall of 2018<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HKzn5BLyID0| title = Henri Poincaire Institute}}</ref> and a Radcliffe Fellow at [[Harvard University]] from 2015 to 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.radcliffe.harvard.edu/people/raul-jimenez| title = Radcliffe Harvard}}</ref>
